text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Russia will stop all transactions in hard currency from October.
- Small regional banks are merging to oppose the influence of big Moscow-based banks.
- St.Petersburg is to launch its own Eurobonds worth $300 million.
- A downward slide in the price of Gazprom shares seems to be a reaction to Boris Yeltsin's latest decree.
- Moscow and Kiev still have many unsolved problems but the "grand treaty" will be signed on Friday.
SEGODNYA
- The government is to appove a number of decrees to toughen its control over vodka production.
- Russian tea importers are predicting a reduction of tea purchases by 10-15 percent as a result of an import duty increase on packaged tea due to come into force on June 1.
NESAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Moscow is trying to establish contacts with the Taleban, which has made big military gains in Afghanistan.
- The text of a long-awaited accord to be signed at Kiev summit is published.
- Russia's infant mortality has been between 17 to 19.9 deaths for every 1,000 births over the last six years.
ROSSIASKAYA GAZETA
- A special government commission is set up to consider the idea of forcing all budget debtors to issue additional shares for open distibution.
PRAVDA-5
- President Yeltsin is going to Kiev to give up the Russian fleet.
- The paper warns Russia's leadership against supporting Taleban fighters.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Moscow has received 66 percent of Russia's foreign investments.
- Moscow police arrested two people accused of blowing up a city bus in December 1994.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
